description: Somos uma equipe desenvolvendo o SOLUM, uma solução AgTech para apoiar agricultores usando dados de observação da Terra da NASA. Nosso objetivo é unir tecnologia, inovação e sustentabilidade para ajudar na tomada de decisões sobre o solo e a rotação de culturas.
summary:
SOLUM — NASA Agricultural Intelligence is a web-based platform designed to support agricultural planning by combining geographic information, historical climate data, and crop calendar analysis.

The platform uses NASA POWER climate data to help users explore environmental conditions, organize agricultural information, and compare crop planning scenarios.

By bringing these resources together in an accessible interface, SOLUM aims to make Earth observation data more useful for agricultural decision-making, encouraging informed planning and more sustainable farming practices.

Developed collaboratively by Luiz, Wellington Tomiyoshi Santos Koga, and Telviniz Guilherme Costa.

SOLUM: Space technology at the service of agriculture.
details:
SOLUM — NASA Agricultural Intelligence

SOLUM is a web application designed to support agricultural planning by bringing together farm property management, field boundaries, historical climate data, and crop calendar comparisons.

Users can register properties, search for municipalities, adjust locations on an interactive map, draw or import field boundaries, and calculate field areas. The platform also retrieves historical climate data from NASA POWER, including precipitation, maximum and minimum temperatures, relative humidity, and solar radiation.

Based on user-provided dates and crop cycle durations, SOLUM compares planning calendars for corn, sorghum, and brachiaria. When the necessary economic information is provided, the system also calculates estimated revenue, costs, and profit margins.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript on the frontend; Node.js and Express on the backend; SQLite for data storage; Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for interactive maps; and Chart.js for data visualization.

SOLUM's creative approach is to integrate geographic information, agricultural field geometry, climate context, and transparent calculations into a single platform.

Its intended impact is to make agricultural information more accessible and support better-informed preliminary planning.

The project was collaboratively developed by Luiz, Wellington Tomiyoshi Santos Koga, and Telviniz Guilherme Costa, whose teamwork contributed to bringing the SOLUM concept to life.

SOLUM does not provide official planting recommendations, weather forecasts, yield predictions, or probabilistic risk models. It is a decision-support prototype and does not replace professional agricultural advice.
